fileReviews.summary: Test coverage was added for a timezone/date-override scenario; no correctness issue in the test itself is supported by the evidence.
The override timezone adjustment in slot generation is plausible from the provided diff, and the gathered evidence does not directly support a concrete bug in this file alone.

New availability filtering introduces concrete regressions: slots can be accepted outside working hours, and all-day date overrides are never recognized because Dayjs objects are compared by reference.
Adding an optional timeZone field to TimeRange is a compatible type change with no direct correctness issue supported by the evidence.

findings.claim: The new fallback working-hours validation computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime`, so it never checks the slot's actual end time. As a result, a slot that starts before `workingHour.endTime` but ends after it is treated as available. For example, a 60-minute slot starting at 16:30 against working hours ending at 17:00 will pass because `end` is incorrectly set to 16:30 instead of 17:30.
findings.title: Working-hours check ignores event duration and can admit slots that overrun availability

findings.claim: The new date-override logic tries to special-case all-day overrides by checking `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`. This compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, which is always false even when they represent the same instant. Any caller relying on `start == end` to mean an all-day override will therefore skip this branch and incorrectly reject slots before/after the override bounds instead of treating the whole day as available.
findings.title: All-day date overrides are never detected because Dayjs instances are compared with ===
